title: Acme Biologics onprem / air-gapped discovery
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-11-15
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 60 minutes
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/fireflies-20251115-acmebio-001 (auto)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Raman (Acme Biologics), Marcus Lee (Acme Biologics, CISO), Anita Gomez (Acme Biologics, Infra)
summary: Initial discovery for air-gapped / on-prem private deployment. Customer is highly regulated (bio-pharma) and requires an offline installer, signed model bundles, proof of KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and a hardware checklist. They want to validate inference latency on their HPE/NVIDIA stack and confirm update process for models and security patches in a disconnected environment. Next step: security pack and offline install artifacts, schedule technical deep dive and benchmarking POC.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2/ISO docs, audit logs spec) by 2025-11-18
SE to share air-gapped installer workflow and hardware checklist by 2025-11-18
Schedule 90-min technical deep-dive + benchmarking with Acme infra team week of 2025-11-24
Customer to share allowed change window and proxy/network constraints
action_items: Sofia Martinez: Send pricing sheet + pilot contract template by 2025-11-18
Ethan Cole: Prepare offline installer checklist and model packaging notes by 2025-11-18
Dr. Priya Raman / Anita Gomez: Share current GPU inventory and networking constraints (list of hosts, NICs, RDMA usage) by 2025-11-20
Marcus Lee: Provide list of required compliance artifacts for procurement review by 2025-11-20
transcript: [00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, I'm Sofia over at Redwood Inference, AE. with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:12] Dr. Priya Raman: Hi Sofia, thanks. I'm Priya, head of MLOps at Acme Biologics. we, um, run models in a highly regulated environment so the air-gapped requirement is kind of a hard constraint.
[00:24] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CISO. yeah security's the priority. we only allow outbound to a corporate proxy and physical media movement for large model weights.
[00:33] Ethan Cole: Got it, thanks. can you give a quick snapshot of your infra? like GPU type, orchestration, and whether k8s is allowed?

[00:38] Anita Gomez: we use HPE servers with NVIDIA A100 40GB, some newer racks have H100 queued for next quarter, we're currently running on-prem Kubernetes but in a very locked down fashion, no egress except through a corporate proxy. we also have a subset of air-gapped labs with zero external access.

[00:52] Sofia Martinez: ok that's super helpful. so we have three deployment models at Redwood: hosted, dedicated, and private. for air-gapped you need our Private on-prem package which supports offline installers, signed bundles, and KMS integrations. quick question — do you need hardware-level HSM integration or will a customer-managed KMS inside the network suffice?
[01:07] Marcus Lee: We prefer an HSM for key wrapping. we have a network HSM in a FIPS mode, we'd want Redwood to support BYO-HSM or at least show how to integrate with our HSM's KMIP endpoint.

[01:20] Ethan Cole: we do BYO-KMS/HSM integrations via KMIP or AWS CloudHSM-compatible APIs for the components that need key unwrapping. for the air-gapped installer we can ship encrypted config that references keys stored in your local HSM — no key material leaves your org.

[01:34] Dr. Priya Raman: ok good. next, how do model updates work? we can't pull from public registries in the lab. we need a way to push model weights and runtime updates via physical media or an approved internal artifact repo.

[01:48] Sofia Martinez: right — our offline workflow supports signed model bundles. you can transfer via USB or secure transfer to an internal S3-like repo, and the installer performs signature verification. updates are batched and we provide an import tool that runs in your air-gapped zone. there are also checksums and provenance metadata included.
[02:03] Anita Gomez: filesize is a concern. some of these checkpoints are hundreds of gigabytes. does the offline installer support staged import and quantized models?

[02:10] Ethan Cole: yes, we have support for sliced model payloads and resumable import. we also provide tooling for quantization recommendations — e.g. 4-bit quantized variants of your model to reduce size and VRAM. that being said, for highest fidelity you might want the fp16 variant on the A100/H100 depending on the workload.
[02:27] Marcus Lee: what about network egress during runtime? can the runtime phone home for telemetry or corpus uploads?

[02:33] Sofia Martinez: for Private on-prem in air-gapped mode, telemetry is fully optional and can be disabled. metrics can be sent to an internal metrics backend; nothing needs to leave your network unless you choose to enable it. we can provide an on-prem observability stack or connect to prometheus/grafana you already have.
[02:48] Dr. Priya Raman: great. performance — we need predictable latency for real-time inference on structured prompts. what kind of latency can we expect on A100 40GB for our 8k-context model?

[02:59] Ethan Cole: depends on model size and batch. ballpark, for a 7B-13B class model optimized with our kernels plus kv-caching you'd see single-digit tens of ms per token for short context if you tune batching; for 70B or larger that goes up. we recommend running a quick in-situ benchmark — we can bring a micro-benchmark to run on your infra during the POC.
[03:18] Anita Gomez: are there kernel-level requirements? we run with Mellanox NICs and RDMA between hosts, and we're curious about GPUDirect / RDMA for cross-node KV cache.

[03:27] Ethan Cole: we support GPUDirect and RDMA-friendly paths in our runtime; pcm config and drivers must be present. we'll provide a hardware checklist — specific linux kernel, CUDA, and driver matrix — to ensure compatibility. cross-node KV syncing typically adds complexity, so for the POC we usually keep model shards on a single node unless you want to do multi-node sharding testing.
[03:47] Marcus Lee: compliance paperwork — SOC2 isn't enough for procurement, they also want ISO27001, penetration test reports, and details on audit logs retention. can you provide those?

[03:58] Sofia Martinez: yes, we'll send our SOC2 report and ISO-appropriate artifacts where available, plus an audit log spec. for Private installs we provide a local audit logger that writes to your SIEM-compatible format. we'll also include an explanation of which telemetry elements are included and how to disable them.
[04:12] Dr. Priya Raman: excellent. licensing / pricing model? we need something predictable for budgeting — reserved capacity or flat license for private install?

[04:20] Sofia Martinez: for Private we offer a platform license (one-time install fee + annual support) or a reserved capacity model for Dedicated. given you are fully air-gapped, Private with an annual subscription plus support SLA is common. I'll send a pilot pricing and contract template after this call.
[04:35] Anita Gomez: patching cadence concerns — we enforce change windows, and we can't accept automatic updates. how are security patches delivered?

[04:41] Ethan Cole: patches are packaged as signed update bundles. you pick accepted versions and schedules; we don't push updates automatically in the air-gapped mode. we also provide provenance metadata and reproducible builds for audit.
[04:55] Marcus Lee: about vulnerability scanning — will the images include SBOMs and be scanable internally?
[04:59] Sofia Martinez: yes, SBOMs for container images and the runtime components are included in the security pack. you can run your internal scanners against them before importing.
[05:09] Dr. Priya Raman: for the POC we want a small pilot: run our model (we'll provide a 13B fine-tuned checkpoint) and run latency/cost benchmarks for a real inference workload. timeline?

[05:19] Sofia Martinez: typically a 4–6 week pilot: week 0 provisioning and verifier, week 1 installer + smoke tests, week 2 benchmarking and tuning, weeks 3–4 iterate and sign-off. for air-gapped starts we sometimes need an extra week for artifact transfer and compliance review.
[05:33] Anita Gomez: transfer mechanism — do you support signed tarballs over SFTP or do you insist on physical disk?

[05:38] Ethan Cole: we support both. signed tarballs for SFTP to an internal repo is common; for very large weights we support physical disk transfer with signed manifests. the important part is signature verification during import.
[05:50] Marcus Lee: there's also procurement / legal items — we need sample contract language for data residency and indemnities. can you share a redlineable contract?
[05:58] Sofia Martinez: yes, I'll share a pilot contract and standard terms. procurement often wants a separate MSA for enterprise installs, we can work with that.
[06:07] Dr. Priya Raman: curious about model hosting options — can we host both vendor-supplied and self-trained models?

[06:12] Ethan Cole: yes both. we support BYO models; you control which models are imported into the private runtime. we'll also help with quantization and model variants to match your latency/cost targets.
[06:23] Sofia Martinez: QA question — do you require RBAC integration with your corporate SSO/AD?
[06:27] Marcus Lee: SSO via SAML2 and AD integration is mandatory. we want RBAC that maps to AD groups.
[06:33] Ethan Cole: we support SAML-based SSO and can sync group membership to RBAC policies locally. we'll include setup steps in the install guide.
[06:41] Anita Gomez: any non-kubernetes deploys? some labs don't allow k8s, they'd prefer a docker-compose or systemd-based install.

[06:48] Ethan Cole: our installer supports Kubernetes and an air-gapped standalone mode using OCI runtimes and systemd units. caveat: some advanced autoscaling paths assume k8s, but we can run single-node or multi-node without k8s for the POC.
[07:02] Dr. Priya Raman: what's the expected ops overhead? our team is small; we'd prefer minimal day-to-day maintenance.

[07:09] Sofia Martinez: we provide runbooks, an optional managed support tier with 24/7 response, and automation for rolling restarts. most customers run with our support during the pilot and then transition to a lower-touch model once benchmarking is stable.
[07:22] Marcus Lee: does Redwood capture prompt or customer data in any way by default? we need guarantees — PHI and other sensitive data must never leave environment.

[07:30] Sofia Martinez: by default in Private air-gapped mode no data leaves the environment. we can also redact or hash certain fields before any optional telemetry. we will document everything in the security pack.
[07:41] Anita Gomez: do you have any internal recommended specs for performance? like for a 13B fine-tuned model with batching of 8, what's a baseline VM footprint?

[07:49] Ethan Cole: for 13B we typically recommend at least 40GB of GPU memory (A100 40GB) with 250GB host memory for batching headroom and fast IO; NVMe for model staging helps. we'll include a recommended hardware worksheet.
[08:02] Dr. Priya Raman: procurement will ask about SLAs — do you offer uptime SLAs for private installs?

[08:07] Sofia Martinez: we offer SLA-backed options as part of our enterprise support add-on; the baseline private license includes support SLAs for response times, and we can contract for higher availability targets depending on architecture and runbook.
[08:20] Marcus Lee: last technical point — can you demo the offline installer on a small VM so we can see the signature verification step?

[08:27] Ethan Cole: yes, that's exactly what we'd propose for the tech deep-dive. we'll demo the installer, the import flow, and a micro-benchmark. that gives you confidence the signed bundles verify correctly in your environment.

[08:38] Sofia Martinez: ok quick recap and next steps: I'll send pricing + pilot contract and the security pack. Ethan will send the offline installer checklist and hardware compatibility matrix. you will share GPU inventory and the formal list of compliance docs you need. propose dates for the technical deep-dive next week. anything else?
[08:54] Dr. Priya Raman: no that's it for now, thanks. one note — can you include a rough estimate of the physical transfer window for 400GB model weights? procurement often asks that.
[09:02] Ethan Cole: yes we'll include transfer time estimates and recommended compression/quantization tradeoffs in the hardware checklist.
[09:10] Marcus Lee: thanks everyone. we'll look out for the security pack and schedule invite for the deep dive.
[09:16] Sofia Martinez: perfect — thanks all, we'll follow up with materials by Tuesday. bye for now.
[59:12] (recording ends)
